intro: GraphSAGE can preserve a node’s own features separately from the average of its neighbors. Concatenating these two signals lets a learned projection treat them differently.
task: Average each node’s neighbors, concatenate self and neighbor features, then apply a projection, ReLU and row normalization. Define isolated-node behavior explicitly.
requirements: adjacency is a nonempty nonnegative (N,N) matrix with zero diagonal. Positive adjacency[i,j] means j is a neighbor of i; edge magnitude is ignored and symmetry is not required.
features is (N,F), weight is (2*F,O), and F,O are positive. Use every listed neighbor, without random sampling. Isolated nodes get a zero neighbor vector.
Concatenate [self_features, neighbor_mean] in that order. Apply ReLU after multiplying by weight, then divide each row by max(L2_norm,1e-8). Return an (N,O) array.
Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, in addition to the bounds above. Leave all inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Separate absence from a zero-valued neighbor
hints.body: An isolated node has no divisor; explicitly produce a zero vector for its aggregate.

hints.title: Check concatenation order
hints.body: The first F rows of weight act on self features and the next F rows act on neighbor features.

explanation: Keeping self and neighbor features separate differs from adding a self loop to one shared average. The learned weight can emphasize either part independently.
Final normalization removes positive scale but preserves direction. A zero row stays zero, and rows with norms below 1e-8 use the denominator floor rather than being forced to unit length.
Adapted the upstream full-neighborhood GraphSAGE path. Removed optional random neighbor sampling and retained its ReLU and 1e-8 norm floor for deterministic browser practice.
